summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA asks whether Micron's crash — down almost 13% on the day, over 25% in five days and almost 35% in a month — is a generational buying opportunity. The trigger is the US midterm election: Democrats took the House and Senate and several local anti-data-centre measures passed, raising fears that data-centre build-outs will slow. He explains why communities resist data centres: unlike a car plant, they create few lasting jobs but consume energy and water and raise local prices, while adding noise and pollution. The shift is a headwind, he concedes, but demand is not going away: hyperscalers still want the capacity, so spending may simply stretch from two or three years to five or six, and AI's cost savings for enterprises keep demand intact. Micron's boom is extraordinary: a record 75% trailing operating margin, above 80% in each of the last two quarters — the first time in eight years of covering thousands of statements he has seen that. The stock is still up sharply in 2026 despite falling nearly 50% from its $1,250 all-time high to about $697. At a forward P/E of 3.4 — versus Tesla at roughly 150 — his fair value is $1,531. Call: MU BUY; he has recently added Micron to his own portfolio and says he may add more.
title: Why Is Micron Stock Crashing, and is it a Generational Buying Opportunity? | MU Stock Analysis
